clue.text: Fabulous son in south-east of country

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: the son letter sits inside the rest, so it signals one piece going into another

parts.note: of a country is national

explanation.surface: A boy from the south-east of some country is said to be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something astonishing or marvellous, in the colloquial praising sense.

clue.text: Ruined castle inhabited by king's shade

indicators.note: the king's letter lives inside the rearranged castle, signalling insertion
a ruined building has its parts knocked about, so the letters of castle are rearranged

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A crumbling fortress has a monarch living in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' turns CASTLE into SCALET; 'inhabited by' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright red, one shade or hue of colour.

clue.text: Turned up brown uniform on character

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone in a brown uniform has arrived, judged on their character.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their temperament or essential disposition.

clue.text: Diarist of Roman emperor leaving out head spy

indicators.note: the leading letter of the emperor's name is dropped

parts.note: Hadrian was the Roman emperor who built the wall across northern England
a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A diary kept by a Roman emperor, minus a spymaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving out head' drops the H of HADRIAN. Adrian Mole is the teenage diarist of Sue Townsend's comic British novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional schoolboy writes his whole story as a journal, making him a famous diary keeper.

clue.text: Rascals regularly hid my post

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one, from the phrase

explanation.surface: Mischief-makers routinely hide someone's mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of HID MY POST give I, M, P, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous children, little scamps or rascals.

clue.text: Told elevated cleric about time with a bishop

indicators.note: the reversed cleric goes round the other letters
in a down clue, elevated means lifted up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A senior churchman, promoted, recounts a story about time spent with a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses DEAN to NAED; 'about' wraps it around RRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to recount or relate it.

clue.text: Cry after the Parisian's attack without restraint

indicators.note: the cry comes after the French article in the answer

parts.note: la is French for the, as a Parisian would say it
to shout is to cry out

explanation.surface: A yell following a Frenchwoman's assault that knows no bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to hit out wildly, physically or verbally, unrestrainedly.

clue.text: Company behind brief for surface protector

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: astern means behind, on a ship

explanation.surface: A firm lagging behind on a short brief about protecting surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of ASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is a small mat set under a glass to protect a table top.

clue.text: Female shooters arrived with harsh warning

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, to arrive
raw weather is harsh and cold
an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: Women gunfighters turned up with a stern caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooters' suggests guns but means people who shoot film.
explanation.definitionFit: Women operating cameras shoot footage, so they are shooters in the filming sense.

clue.text: Studied South American country's education

parts.note: Peru with its possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone researched the schooling system of a nation in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully, so the past tense means studied.

clue.text: Stroke and massage podgy dad with gel

indicators.note: to massage is to knead and work, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rub a chubby father with ointment and stroke him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a caress beside 'massage', but it is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple swimming style, paddling the hands like a dog, is a stroke in the swimming sense.

clue.text: Feverish strain, jammed in shopping centre

indicators.note: the tune is pushed inside the shopping centre

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
a strain is a tune, and an aria is a solo song

explanation.surface: Someone feels flushed and stressed, wedged in a crowded mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria causes recurring fevers, so the related adjective suggests feverish.

clue.text: Garment when reversed, reportedly not right

indicators.note: the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: what is heard spoken, so a word sounding like the one meant

parts.note: wrong is the opposite of right

explanation.surface: An item of clothing put on back to front, said to be incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns AS to SA; 'reportedly' gives RONG, said like WRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrap of cloth worn around the waist, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Made regular deals with minor criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Business dealings with an underage lawbreaker were made routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise something is to bring it to a standard or regular state.

clue.text: Rank rodent close to hole

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A foul rodent near its burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective, foul, but it is the verb to rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank something is to grade or rate it.

clue.text: Boastfully misrepresented my old times

indicators.note: presented wrongly, so the letters are given in a false order

explanation.surface: Someone bragged and falsely described their former days.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without modesty means talking oneself up, which is boasting.

clue.text: Ring found in sink quietly put on ear

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
lughole is British slang for ear

explanation.surface: A ring found in the sink was quietly placed on someone's ear, like an earring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places P on top of LUGHOLE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The drain hole in a basin is a round opening, a ring found in the sink.

clue.text: Wide part of foot caught by light immobilising device

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
the heel is part of the foot
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: A broad foot snared by a lamp, as if trapped in a device.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheel clamp is fixed to an illegally parked car's wheel so it cannot be driven away.
explanation.definitionFit: The clamp locks a car wheel in place, a device that stops the vehicle moving.

clue.text: Blow up general in conflict

indicators.note: the letters are at war with each other, thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An army general explodes in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' suggests an explosion, but it means to magnify a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger, to magnify it.

clue.text: Furniture one's removed from capital city

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of the city name

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
I is the roman numeral for one; one's means one is

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture has been moved out of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I out of SOFIA leaves SOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is a long upholstered seat, a piece of household furnishing.

clue.text: Figure running to span court with ace shot

indicators.note: to span is to stretch across, so the outer piece goes round the rest

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
A is the card abbreviation for ace
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A figure sprints across a tennis court after an ace serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to span' puts ON either side of CTAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided geometric figure.

clue.text: Toast with superior gold colour

indicators.note: superior means higher up, so in this down clue the gold sits above the toast

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to burn bread is to toast it too far

explanation.surface: Golden toast with an excellent colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown shade, usually of hair.

clue.text: Mass celebration around a Mediterranean resort

parts.note: M is the physics abbreviation for mass

indicators.note: turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

explanation.surface: A church service and a party surrounding something at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks as if it wraps the A, but it signals reading the celebration backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Málaga is a city and resort on Spain's Costa del Sol, beside the Mediterranean.

clue.text: US agent carrying large relative showed off

indicators.note: the agent holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in US slang
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: An American federal agent carried a big relation and made a display of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to display it ostentatiously, to parade it.

clue.text: Like Ibiza on vacation, or far bigger place?

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: vacating the word empties it, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A holiday spot such as Ibiza, or somewhere much larger?
explanation.walkthrough: Ibiza emptied out leaves IA. Asia is a continent, far bigger than any island.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole continent is a place much larger than a Balearic island.

clue.text: Ravenous itinerant dropping skinned rat in a stew

indicators.note: an itinerant wanders about, so the letters roam out of order
the letter is dropped from the word
with its skin, the outer letters, removed, leaving only the middle

explanation.surface: A starving wanderer throws out a peeled rat from the casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' leaves A from RAT; 'dropping' takes it out of RAVENOUS, leaving RVENOUS, which 'itinerant' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being anxious and agitated.

clue.text: Illegally bring in small vessel, finally evading all police

parts.note: a mug is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: Sneak contraband in a little boat, at last escaping the whole police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a cup. The last letters of 'evading all police' give G, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To smuggle is to import goods secretly and unlawfully.

clue.text: Occasionally sitting in the veranda nonchalantly

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Every so often someone lounges on the porch, cool as anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic phrase for now and again, from time to time.
